feed.title: Vx
feed.subtitle: Notes on building Vx, a heterogeneous-systems programming language.

entry.title: Tiles, without a tile type
entry.summary: Can Vx be used for tile-based GPU programming, the way NVIDIA's cuTile is? A block loop, a tensor in Memory::SMEM and two barriers already compile to PTX with shared storage and bar.sync. What Vx adds is that the tile's memory space is part of its type and its shared-memory budget is a compile error; what it lacks is everything that makes a tile a value.

entry.title: What writing core taught the compiler
entry.summary: A week ago Vx had no core library. Now it has six modules of it, a random-number library, and the compiler fixes that writing them forced, a method that dispatched differently between runs among them. Every line is Vx, with no extern in it.

entry.title: The NUMA that wasn't there
entry.summary: A CPU's NUMA domains are the same relation as two GPUs on a node, so modelling them needed no new machinery. The compiler predicted a remote access costs 2.26x a local one and the hardware said 2.35x — after a day of measurements taken on a machine that reports two NUMA nodes it does not have.

entry.title: What a pointer forgets
entry.summary: A function stages a tensor to the GPU and returns it. In C++ the return type is float * and the fact is gone at the boundary. In Vx the memory space is part of the type, so the return type carries it.

entry.title: Vx 0.0.1: placement in the type system
entry.summary: The first Vx release. What the compiler checks, what it runs on, and the parts that are honestly not built yet.
